title: One slice's life: from planned to merged, failed for good or replaced
description: A planned slice is written, then tested unless there are no tests to run (no test command, or only prose changed in a git repository), then reviewed. Failing tests, or a bugfix slice without a test that fails before the fix, send it back to writing. A failed review's gaps are validated by a fresh reviewer: confirmed gaps send the slice back to writing for its second attempt (the same writer, resumed) or its third and last (a fresh writer on Opus); when none stand, the slice counts as passed. The same gap in two failed reviews in a row stalls the slice, and a replan replaces it; if the run already had its replan, or three attempts fail, the slice has failed for good. A passed slice is merged into the result branch.

nodes.label: Testing
nodes.detail: A bugfix needs a failing test first

edges.label: no tests to run
sources: src/orchestrator.ts (the tests run only when a test command is given)

edges.label: confirmed: retry
sources: .claude/agents/orchestrator.md step 6 (second attempt: SendMessage resume; third: fresh implementer on opus)

edges.label: same gap twice in a row
sources: .claude/rules/agents.md (stall gate: two consecutive failed reviews share a gap key)

edges.label: replan used
sources: .claude/agents/orchestrator.md step 6 (if the run already had its replan, the slice has failed for good)

notes: A failed review: a failed checked id or a gap of 80 or more; lower gaps pass with a doubt signal. When no gap stands, the passing validation is the latest review and an Opus review must still pass the slice.

Validating, the resume and the Opus third attempt are native and workflow steps; the stall (replan_required) is native only. The SDK pipeline sends gaps straight back, up to --retries, and replans only with --replans N.
A replan runs at most once per run; replaced slices are never merged.

The test step runs only when a test command exists. Natively, verify.sh also skips it, in a git work tree with ORCH_TEST_CMD unset, when every changed path is prose (no_code_changes), and then the slice goes straight to review. Its bugfix check (KIND: bugfix) needs a test that fails on the base and passes now.
